title: arxiv_2105.09397v1
universal_lens: Multilayer network models unify heterogeneous relational ties through shared node spaces, enabling cross-layer influence analysis in complex socio-criminal systems. Tensorial adjacency representations unify network topology and node-state dynamics via canonical basis projections and covariant contravariant components.
gsi_mapping: Bayesian belief updates on node centrality across multilayer criminal networks utilize conformal predictive distributions for robust actor identification under uncertainty. Bayesian inference on network states uses tensorial adjacency models to update belief distributions over node degrees and interconnectivity.
gse_mapping: Situationally-aware state transitions in GSE track actor movement and communication patterns across network layers to predict operational vulnerabilities. Situational reasoning maps node transitions through multilayer adjacency tensors, enabling state-space traversal and predictive trajectory synthesis.

primitives.name: Multilayer Network Structure
primitives.verbatim_quote: Recently, Social Network Analysis studies have led to an improvement and to a generalization of existing tools to networks with multiple subsystems and layers of connectivity.
primitives.assumptions: Networks consist of multiple interdependent layers sharing common nodes; each layer represents a distinct type of relationship or interaction.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When layer interdependence diminishes, the system reverts to single-layer analysis.

layer2.mapping: The multilayer structure maps to GSI's probabilistic graphical model where each layer corresponds to a conditional probability distribution over shared entities.
layer2.telemetry: Node degree distribution across layers and inter-layer edge density.

primitives.name: Multiplex Network Definition
primitives.verbatim_quote: Multilayer networks in which each layer shares at least one node with some other layer in the network are called multiplex networks.
primitives.assumptions: All nodes must appear in at least two layers; inter-layer connectivity enables cross-layer influence propagation.
primitives.breakdown_regime: If no shared nodes exist, the network becomes a stack of independent layers.

layer2.mapping: Multiplex kernel emerges in GSE as a composite adjacency matrix encoding simultaneous interactions across layers.
layer2.telemetry: Overlap ratio of nodes across layers and inter-layer clustering coefficient.

primitives.name: Criminal Network Model
primitives.verbatim_quote: In this paper, we built a criminal multiplex network which concerns an anti-mafia operation called "Montagna" and it is based on the examination of a pre-trial detention order issued on March 14, 2007 by the judge for preliminary investigations of the Court of Messina (Sicily).
primitives.assumptions: Criminal networks exhibit layered communication and interaction patterns; key actors are identified via centrality measures in multilayer contexts.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Model fails when data integrity is compromised or when layers lack meaningful overlap.

layer2.mapping: The criminal multiplex model aligns with GSI’s Bayesian inference framework for identifying high-influence nodes in adversarial environments.
layer2.telemetry: Number of identified key actors and their inter-layer connectivity scores.

primitives.name: Node Importance Measure in Multilayer Networks
primitives.verbatim_quote: We followed three different approaches to measure the importance of nodes in multilayer networks using degree as descriptor.
primitives.assumptions: Node importance is quantified via aggregated degree across layers; higher degrees indicate greater influence or centrality.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When node degree is uniform across layers, significance becomes ambiguous without additional metrics.

layer2.mapping: The derived kernel in GSE computes a multilayer centrality score combining intra- and inter-layer degrees for dynamic actor prioritization.
layer2.telemetry: Average multilayer degree per node and variance in layer-specific degrees.

primitives.verbatim_quote: It is possible to define some descriptive measures able to highlight particular characteristics of a network.

primitives.breakdown_regime: When node is isolated (d(v_i)=0) or fully connected (d(v_i)=N-1).

layer2.mapping: Degree vector derived from adjacency tensor via column summation; enables centrality analysis in GSI.
layer2.telemetry: Node degree distribution across network layers.

primitives.breakdown_regime: When vector space dimensionality changes or basis becomes non-orthonormal.

primitives.name: Multiplex Network Topology
primitives.verbatim_quote: Starting from the Meetings and Phone Calls simple graphs, we created an undirected and weighted multilayer network with two layers called Meetings and Phone Calls, 154 nodes and 439 edges (see Fig.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Nodes ($N=154$, dimensionless count), Edges ($E=439$, dimensionless count), Layers ($L=2$, dimensionless categorical index)
primitives.assumptions: The system can be abstracted into discrete entities (nodes) interacting via distinct, non-interchangeable channels (layers). Interactions are symmetric (undirected) and cumulative (weighted).
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails when interactions are strictly asymmetric (requiring directed hypergraphs) or when temporal dynamics invalidate the static snapshot assumption.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic mapping to GSI multi-sensor fusion: Layer 1 = Biomechanical tracking, Layer 2 = Audio/Comms tracking. Shared nodes = Athletes present in both datasets.
layer2.telemetry: Node overlap ratio (47 shared nodes / 154 total nodes).

primitives.name: Interlayer Node Overlap
primitives.verbatim_quote: There were 47 individuals who jointly belonged to both graphs.
primitives.assumptions: Identity resolution across layers is perfect; a node in Layer 1 is unequivocally identifiable as its counterpart in Layer 2.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down under aliasing or identity fragmentation where a single actor uses multiple unlinked identities across layers.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSE 'Active Agent' kernel. Only nodes existing in both spatial and communication layers are considered fully active decision-makers in the situational model.

primitives.name: Edge Weight Accumulation
primitives.verbatim_quote: The weight encodes the number of meetings or phone calls.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Weight ($w_{ij}^{\alpha}$, dimensionless frequency count), Interaction indicator ($\mathbb{I}$, boolean)
primitives.assumptions: Interaction frequency is a valid proxy for relationship strength or dependency intensity. Events are independent and additive.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Invalid if interactions exhibit diminishing returns or if negative interactions (conflicts) cancel out positive ones without explicit signed weighting.

layer2.mapping: GSI mapping to 'Chemistry Score'. Edge weights between players accumulate based on successful pass completions or proximal time spent, driving the Bayesian prior for future coordination.

primitives.name: Aggregate Network Importance
primitives.verbatim_quote: We wanted to perform an analysis of suspects' importance for each layer separately, for the aggregate network and the multilayer one which allowed to quantify the importance across the whole series of layers.
primitives.assumptions: Importance is derived from combined layer contributions; normalized across all layers.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When individual layer importance is low but aggregate is high, indicates bridging role.

primitives.name: Multilayer Centrality Ranking
primitives.verbatim_quote: We showed the top 20 characters ranked by their degree in each layer, in the aggregate network and in the multilayer network comparing the resulting importance with the role they had in the Sicilian Mafia families which were the protagonists of the "Montagna" operation.

reasoning_traces.think: The derivation of sovereign primitives from this chapter window hinges on the transition from isolated simple graphs to a cohesive multiplex network. Initially, the criminal ecosystem is decomposed into two disjoint topological spaces: the Meetings graph ($G_M$) and the Phone Calls graph ($G_P$). While $G_M$ captures high-fidelity, high-risk physical interactions, $G_P$ encapsulates low-friction, asynchronous communications. The mathematical leap occurs when these are fused into a multilayer network $M$. This is not merely a union of edges, but a stratification where the identity of a node persists across layers, yet its connectivity profile is layer-dependent. The primitive 'Multiplex Network Topology' formalizes this stratification. The 'Interlayer Node Overlap' primitive isolates the subset of actors who are polymorphic, operating in both physical and digital domains. In the context of Galaxy Sports Intelligence, this mirrors the integration of biomechanical tracking (physical presence) with audio/video comms (digital presence). The 'Edge Weight Accumulation' primitive provides the metric for relationship intensity, assuming that frequency correlates with dependency. Finally, 'Multilayer Degree Centrality' aggregates these weighted connections to identify pivotal actors. The table of top-ranked nodes demonstrates that high centrality in the aggregate network often correlates with high-ranking roles (Caporegime, Associate), validating the use of topological metrics to infer hierarchical importance. This doctrinal shift—from analyzing siloed interactions to analyzing the multiplex topology—allows for a more robust identification of key influencers who might be obscured if only one layer were examined.
reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: This methodology traces its lineage to the early 20th-century development of social network analysis by Jacob Moreno, who introduced sociograms to map interpersonal relations. However, the specific formalization of multiplex networks emerges from the late 2000s work of Alex Arenas and Santo Fortunato, who extended traditional graph theory to handle interdependent layers. The application to criminal networks builds upon earlier law enforcement efforts to map mafia structures using single-layer graphs, recognizing that modern illicit organizations operate across multiple communication channels simultaneously. The shift to multilayer analysis acknowledges that an actor's importance cannot be reduced to a single mode of interaction.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: Modeling the opposing agents (the criminals) requires understanding their strategic use of multiple channels. A Caporegime does not rely solely on meetings because they are risky; they do not rely solely on calls because they are insecure. They optimize their behavior by distributing interactions across layers to maximize operational security while maintaining control. The 'Entrepreneur' or 'Pharmacist' appearing high in the rankings suggests they serve as critical bridges (brokers) between the core criminal families and external resources. Their high degree in the aggregate network indicates they are trusted nodes in both physical and digital spheres, a rare and valuable attribute that the network exploits.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: A critical anti-collinearity check must be applied when fusing layers. If the Meetings and Phone Calls graphs were perfectly collinear (i.e., every meeting was followed by a call and vice versa), the multiplex structure would collapse into a single weighted graph, rendering the layer distinction meaningless. The veto condition arises if the correlation between layer-specific degrees is too high, suggesting redundant information rather than complementary insights. Furthermore, leakage occurs if the identity resolution fails, causing a single individual to be counted as multiple nodes across layers, artificially inflating the network size and distorting centrality metrics. The 47 overlapping nodes out of 154 total nodes indicate a significant but not total overlap, preserving the multiplex nature and ensuring that the derived primitives capture genuine multimodal complexity.
